requiredFindings.problem: Reader membership is suppressed only for the CLI tier. A discovery.workspaceRoots array from the project or local layer still lets cargo-config-patch@1 and npm-workspaces-members@1 add members, which widens a supplied root list.
requiredFindings.evidence: Item 20 labels the CLI as Explicit and the config array as Config, then says only an explicit source suppresses reader membership. NE:919-921 restricts discovery for both Config2 workspaceRoots and --workspace-root to exactly those roots and forbids widening them into a scan. SLM:774-785 is if/elif/else: a config array does not fall through to automatic discovery. AQ:115 selects automatic discovery only when the array is omitted. S3's content is items 19, 20, 22, and 24, and its cell names the Config2 join, so copying item 20 as written would drop that exact-roots rule for the config tier.
requiredFindings.fix: State that a present admitted discovery.workspaceRoots array, from the config layer or from --workspace-root, suppresses reader membership. Readers may still record links whose directories lie inside members that array already admitted. Readers declare members only when the array is absent. Keep exactly-those-roots, never widened, in the Config2-join text S3 edits.

nonBlockingObservations.location: PROPOSAL.md item 12, the census-margin rule, and item 19's member byte bound
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The census counts directories and entries outside pruned segments. The 2^30 byte cap is not part of that count. The separate bound of 64 members, each at most 4 MiB of index and 64 KiB of config (X2:272), is what puts bytes under the cap. The return-to-law rule covers a census miss.
